subject.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts

question: Should QQBot adopt the same fixed 30-second body-idle failure policy as sibling media channels for all adapter and file-download callers?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility and availability tradeoff, not a mechanical implementation question: it prevents indefinite resource retention while changing how unusually delayed upstream media bodies fail.

options.title: Accept shared policy
options.body: Approve the 120-second header and 30-second idle defaults for QQBot so stalled downloads fail predictably across all current callers.

options.title: Choose QQBot-specific behavior
options.body: Keep the shared implementation shape but set a different documented QQBot policy if operational evidence shows the sibling timeout is unsuitable.

options.title: Pause policy change
options.body: Defer the fail-closed default and retain current behavior until QQBot traffic characteristics or owner expectations are established.

recommendation.title: Accept shared policy
recommendation.body: Approve the 120-second header and 30-second idle defaults for QQBot so stalled downloads fail predictably across all current callers.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only concrete recent contributor identified in the supplied history, though a channel owner should make the final policy decision.
